stories.title: Goodfire: most LLM neurons have one job, challenging polysemanticity
stories.summary: Nick Cammarata, who started OpenAI's interpretability team and is now at Goodfire, reports that about 90% of neurons in Qwen-32B are monosemantic, so models can be studied directly without a second model to unfold them.

top_posts.author: @nickcammarata
top_posts.text: interpretability might be the most important scientific problem in the world right now, as I don't think we can solve alignment if we don't know what we're building. I think I have good news about it. I co-authored early work in mechanistic interpretability at OpenAI and came awa

top_posts.author: @deedydas
top_posts.text:
This is one of the most important results in AI, period.

TLDR: neural networks are not tangled knots (polysemanticity is wrong). You can study their own neurons directly, without first "unfolding" them with a second model. 90% of neurons in Qwen-32B have one job.

Nick Cammarata

top_posts.author: @teortaxesTex
top_posts.text:
Very big if true, and a massive dunk on Anthropic's published and much-hyped Science of Interpretability (which Nick is also an author of. So cool of him to go further). Neurons are meaningfully monosemantic. 
My prediction for Goodfire is looking good. https://t.co/p46GxyPLA2
